title: Finite coherent direct image and generic rank for a dominant proper curve map
statement:
Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field], let $X,Y$ be separated integral schemes of finite type and dimension one over $k$ [def-pc-curve], and assume both are proper over $k$ [def-weil-proper-morphism]. Let $f:X\to Y$ be a $k$-morphism with dense image. Equip the function field $k(X)$ with its $k(Y)$-algebra structure induced by the generic stalk map of $f$ [def-sc-function-field, def-sfb-dominant-function-field-map]. Suppose this field extension is finite, and put $d=[k(X):k(Y)]=\dim_{k(Y)}k(X)$ [def-pc-field-tower]. Let $\eta_Y$ be the generic point of $Y$ [def-sc-generic-point], and let $\mathcal F=f_*\mathcal O_X$, where $\mathcal F(V)=\Gamma(f^{-1}V,\mathcal O_X)$ with its $\mathcal O_Y$-action induced by $f^\sharp$ [def-pc-module-pullback]. Then $X,Y$ are Noetherian, meaning quasi-compact and locally Noetherian [pqf-def-locnoeth, def-weil-pbc-quasi-compact-scheme]. The morphism $f$ is finite, hence affine [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism]. The structure modules $\mathcal O_X,\mathcal O_Y$ and $\mathcal F$ are coherent [pqf-def-coherent]. Moreover $\mathcal F$ has generic rank $d$, meaning
$$\dim_{k(Y)}\mathcal F_{\eta_Y}=d,$$
where the stalk and scalar action are those of module sheaves [def-weil-pbc-module-stalk]. Neither smoothness, normality, flatness of $f$, nor separability of the extension is assumed.

source.place: Tag 0AYZ, lemma-degree-pullback-map-proper-curves, first proof sentence: finiteness and coherence of the direct image with rank equal to the function-field degree.

proof.text: The field $k$ is Noetherian: its only ideals are $(0)$ and $(1)$. Thus the one-chart scheme $\operatorname{Spec}k$ is locally Noetherian by the definition, and is quasi-compact by the definition of quasi-compactness, since its space has one point. Apply the finite-type-over-Noetherian theorem to the two structure morphisms, which are finite type by hypothesis. Both $X$ and $Y$ are Noetherian in the required sense.

The proper-over-separated theorem, applied over $\operatorname{Spec}k$, makes $f$ proper. Its image is closed because proper includes universally closed (take the identity base change). The image is also dense by hypothesis, so $f(X)=Y$. The dimension of a curve is the supremum of the Krull dimensions of its local rings; by the local-ring dimension theorem this equals the Krull dimension of the underlying topological space. Hence $\dim X=1\le1$ in the topological sense required below, and $\dim Y=1$ gives a chain $Z_0\subsetneq Z_1$ of irreducible closed subsets of $Y$, so $Y$ has at least two points. Since $X$ is integral, its only irreducible component is $X$ itself. Hence $f$ does not contract its dimension-one component. Apply the noncontraction finiteness theorem: $X$ is proper of dimension at most one and $Y$ is separated over $k$, so $f$ is finite. It is affine by the definition of finite.

On an affine chart $\operatorname{Spec}A$ the structure module is $\widetilde A$, so it is quasi-coherent; it is generated by $1$, so is of finite type. The coherence criterion on the now locally Noetherian schemes $X,Y$ therefore gives coherence of $\mathcal O_X,\mathcal O_Y$. Apply finite-pushforward coherence to the finite map $f$ and the coherent module $\mathcal O_X$, with locally Noetherian target $Y$. This proves that $\mathcal F=f_*\mathcal O_X$ is coherent.

Choose a nonempty affine open $V=\operatorname{Spec}A$ of $Y$. Its inverse image $U$ is nonempty since $f$ is surjective, and is affine since $f$ is finite; write $U=\operatorname{Spec}B$. The map $\varphi=f^\sharp(V):A\to B$ makes $B$ finite over $A$. The affine function-field theorem makes $A,B$ domains and identifies the generic germ maps $a\mapsto a_\eta$ and $b\mapsto b_\xi$ with fraction-field embeddings into $k(Y)$ and $k(X)$, respectively. Write $i:k(Y)\to k(X)$ for the specified generic stalk map. By the definition of a morphism of sheaves, taking a generic germ commutes with $f^\sharp$, so $\varphi(a)_\xi=i(a_\eta)$. Both field and generic-germ maps are injective; hence $\varphi$ is injective.

The generic point of $V=\operatorname{Spec}A$ is its zero prime: $A$ is a domain and the closure of $(0)$ consists of all primes. Apply the affine-pushforward stalk calculation at $\eta_Y$. With $C=\mathcal F_{\eta_Y}$ and $S=\varphi(A\setminus\{0\})$, it says that the actual germ $j:B\to C$ is localization at $S$. In particular the $A$-action is the given action through $f^\sharp$, not an independently chosen scalar structure.

source.place: Tag 0AVW, lemma-affine-morphism-equivalence, proof paragraph beginning Assume Y = Spec(B) and X = Spec(A)

proof.text: Since $B$ is finite over $A$, the finite-algebra integrality theorem makes $B$ integral over $A$. Apply the integral-localization fraction comparison to $\varphi:A\hookrightarrow B$, the localization $j:B\to C$, and the generic-germ embedding $B\hookrightarrow k(X)$. It gives a bijective ring map $q:C\to k(X)$ with $q(j(b)/j(\varphi(a)))=b_\xi/i(a_\eta)$ for $a\ne0$. Every $\lambda\in k(Y)$ is $a_\eta/a'_\eta$ with $a'\ne0$. Its action on $C$ is multiplication by $j(\varphi(a))/j(\varphi(a'))$, because $\mathcal F$ has the specified sheaf-module action. The formula for $q$ sends this multiplier to $i(\lambda)$. Hence $q(\lambda c)=i(\lambda)q(c)$ for every $c\in C$, so $q$ is an isomorphism of $k(Y)$-vector spaces for the specified generic-stalk algebra structure.

source.place: Tag 00GS, lemma-integral-over-field (2), with the explicit fraction-comparison node; finite integrality is Tag 00GK, lemma-finite-is-integral

proof.text: The isomorphism just constructed gives $\dim_{k(Y)}\mathcal F_{\eta_Y}=\dim_{k(Y)}k(X)=d$ by transporting any basis. This is the asserted generic rank. The argument used only integrality, properness, dimension one and the given finite extension; it made no smoothness, normality, flatness or separability assumption.
